method: Primary-source arXiv abstract/history and version-pinned PDFs; pdftotext -layout. Public source downloads only, inherited proxy/TLS retained; no model/API calls.

sources.title: A Calculus for Flow-Limited Authorization

claims.locator: Abstract and Section 1, printed pp.1-2; extracted text lines 20-35, 50-62
claims.claim: Authorization decisions based on sensitive membership lists and passwords can compromise confidentiality; schemes may fundamentally require disclosure, which must be identified.

claims.locator: Section 5, printed p.14; extracted text lines 873-877
claims.claim: Authorization proofs can themselves form a side channel. FLAC protects proof confidentiality while other data policies are modified.

claims.locator: Section 1, printed p.3; extracted text lines 132-140; references [7],[9], printed p.33
claims.claim: 2021 report strengthens and corrects earlier FLAC (CSF 2016) and builds on FLAM (CSF 2015); authorization-flow interaction is established prior work.

sources.scope: Formal language/type-system guarantees; no LLM-agent collusion experiments. Cover says technical report April 22, 2021; arXiv submission/history is April 21.

sources.title: The LLMbda Calculus: AI Agents, Conversations, and Information Flow

claims.locator: Section 1, printed p.2; extracted text lines 86-92
claims.claim: An untracked Python retry loop outside CaMeL IFC reveals a secret-dependent policy-block/termination bit; adaptive reruns can launder the secret one bit at a time. The paper explicitly identifies this control-boundary failure and cites multi-run security.

claims.locator: Section 4.2, printed pp.13-15; extracted text lines 606-701
claims.claim: Proves termination-insensitive probabilistic noninterference (TIPNI), not termination-sensitive noninterference; compatibility rather than equal endpoint subdistributions is central.

claims.locator: Section 7.1, printed p.20; extracted text lines 961-969
claims.claim: An internal retry loop carries taint from a failed attempt into the next attempt and hence into the final plan.

sources.scope: Formal Lean calculus/interpreter plus AgentDojo banking evaluation; exact prior art for denial/retry leakage. Current theorem intentionally permits termination leakage.

sources.title: AgentSecBench: Measuring Prompt Injection, Privacy Leakage, and Tool-Use Integrity in LLM Agents

claims.locator: Section 3.2, printed p.5, Definitions 2-3; extracted text lines 201-225
claims.claim: Defines intent-to-execution noninterference with permitted leakage and confidentiality leakage I(S;Y | authorized leakage, trusted inputs, policy). A zero canary result is not proof of zero information leakage.

claims.locator: Section 4.6, printed p.11; extracted text lines 529-538
claims.claim: One designated marker and one observation intervention; adaptive multi-turn adversaries and obfuscated encodings are outside the evaluated class.

claims.locator: Section 10, printed p.18; extracted text lines 901-915
claims.claim: Exact-marker non-emission establishes resistance only to the chosen distinguisher; multistep plans, mixed authority, semantic encodings and larger models remain outside claims.

sources.scope: Six defense classes with Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B; paired adversarial/benign controls; lexical utility proxy.

sources.title: If Agents Were Angels, No Governance Would Be Necessary: Out-of-Band Policy Enforcement at a Trusted Tool Boundary

claims.locator: Abstract; Section 8.1, printed pp.12-13; extracted text lines 774-816
claims.claim: Four protected email reconstructions occurred without exact field exposure. One trial used increasingly selective predicates over a masked email field and returned row counts as an oracle.

claims.locator: Section 8.1, printed p.13; extracted text lines 806-816
claims.claim: Structural absence from one execution is not relational noninterference. Suggested defenses include coarsened counts/cursors, minimum cohorts and history-aware query budgets; none is evaluated.

claims.locator: Section 10.1, printed p.13; extracted text lines 814 onward
claims.claim: Warnings may themselves reveal the existence of protected data. Timing, aggregate execution, durable approval dispatch and broader deployment paths are outside the released evaluation.

sources.scope: Out-of-band trusted tool boundary; does not claim to close row-count oracle or prove general noninterference. Defensive follow-on should compare scope with these limitations.

sources.title: Nonmalleable Progress Leakage

claims.locator: Abstract and Section 1, printed p.1; extracted text lines 1-39
claims.claim: Progress-insensitive noninterference permits termination behavior leakage, potentially arbitrary leakage within a run or across automatic restarts. Separates attacker-controlled progress leakage from approved progress downgrades.

claims.locator: Section 1, printed p.2; extracted text lines 91-106
claims.claim: Defines nonmalleable progress leakage and gives a type system with Rocq-verified theorems and inference for safe progress downgrades.

sources.scope: General formal IFC foundation; no claim to be an LLM-agent-specific collusion experiment.

novelty_constraint: Do not claim first discovery of authorization/denial/termination/retry leakage. A defensible contribution is an incremental controlled empirical evaluation and bounded mitigation under explicit observables and schedules.
